patches.rationale: slugify currently lowercases and replaces non-[a-z0-9] runs with dashes, but accented characters like 'é' are non-ASCII and get replaced by dashes, producing wrong slugs. Fix: NFKD-normalize, drop combining marks, then apply the existing lowercase/replace/strip pipeline unchanged so ASCII behavior is preserved. Add a new regression test file covering precomposed, decomposed, ASCII separation, dash trimming, and output charset.

review_results.summary: The candidate modifies slugs.py to normalize input with NFKD, strip combining marks, then apply the existing lowercase/non-alphanumeric-to-dash/trim logic. This satisfies the issue's core requirement: 'Café déjà vu' -> 'cafe-deja-vu', decomposed combining acute matches precomposed, ASCII separation preserved, dashes trimmed, and new regression tests added. Regression evidence shows the three key tests failed on original source and pass on the candidate.
concerns: The issue's literal example 'decomposed cafe + combining acute should match precomposed café' is covered by test_decomposed_combining_acute_input and test_precomposed_and_decomposed_match, both witnessed failing on baseline and passing on candidate.
No concerns about type/rounding semantics: slugify still returns str, and the change only adds normalization/stripping before the existing pipeline.

contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_precomposed_accented_input asserts slugify("Caf\u00e9 d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu") == "cafe-deja-vu"; regression_evidence shows this test failed on baseline ('caf-d-j-vu') and passed on candidate (8 passed).

contract_checks.requirement: Decomposed 'cafe' + combining acute (U+0301) should match precomposed 'café'.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_decomposed_combining_acute_input asserts slugify("cafe\u0301 de\u0301ja\u0300 vu") == "cafe-deja-vu"; baseline failed ('cafe-de-ja-vu'), candidate passed.

contract_checks.requirement: Precomposed and decomposed forms of the same text produce identical slug output.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_precomposed_and_decomposed_match asserts slugify(precomposed) == slugify(decomposed); baseline failed, candidate passed.

contract_checks.requirement: Output contains only lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and dashes.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_output_is_lowercase_ascii_digits_and_dashes checks isinstance(result, str) and all(ch.isascii() and (ch.islower() or ch.isdigit() or ch == '-')). Candidate implementation strips combining marks and applies re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ...), guaranteeing ASCII-only output.

contract_checks.requirement: ASCII word separation is preserved: spaces and non-alphanumeric characters become single dashes between words.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_ascii_word_separation_preserved asserts slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world" and slugify("Hello   World") == "hello-world". The regex re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", ...) collapses runs to a single dash, unchanged from original.

contract_checks.requirement: Leading and trailing dashes are trimmed from the result.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_leading_and_trailing_dashes_trimmed asserts slugify("  Hello World  ") == "hello-world" and slugify("---Hello World---") == "hello-world". The .strip("-") call is preserved.

contract_checks.requirement: Existing slugify behavior for pure-ASCII inputs is unchanged.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py::test_pure_ascii_behavior_unchanged asserts slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world", slugify("") == "", slugify("already-slugged") == "already-slugged". tests/test_contract.py::test_existing_contract also asserts slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world" and slugify("") == "". NFKD normalization is a no-op for pure ASCII, so behavior is preserved.

contract_checks.requirement: New regression tests are added covering the accented and decomposed cases.
contract_checks.evidence: tests/test_slugify_unicode.py is a new file with 7 tests covering precomposed, decomposed, equivalence, ASCII-only output, word separation, dash trimming, and pure-ASCII behavior. Regression evidence confirms 3 of these failed on baseline and all 8 passed on candidate.
